summary: On the TCP transport with the durable authority ledger, the master remembers every recovery-purged owner as {node, slot} ('dead ids never return') and treats any record whose SLOT matches a purged slot as belonging to the dead node: dlm_owner_purged() returned true on a slot match alone. Heartbeat slots are reused by later mounts, so once any node has died (or departed) on slot N and been purged at a master, every later occupant of slot N is poisoned at that master: on the next page (re)import (any membership change re-keys the generation and re-imports) its ACTIVE ex record and its shared bits are handed to the 'lazy retirement' path, which runs mxfs_dlm_ledger_purge_owner(<live node>, N) and RETIRES THE LIVE NODE'S DURABLE RECORDS FROM THE PLATTER while it still believes it holds them; a waiter is then granted EX over the same resource — concurrent EX on a live cluster (metadata corruption class), and the live holder's later release goes -ESTALE. On the rig every failed/remounted node during the 0.34.0/0.35.0 formation storms reused a purged slot (P-TAUTH-PURGE-OWNER slots 7,8,11,12,13,20), so this poisoning was active there too.
mechanism: dlm/dlm.c dlm_owner_purged(ctx, node, slot): `if (slot >= 0 && ctx->purged_owners[i].slot == slot) return true;` — the slot clause (sess422, meant for shared bits whose owner the heartbeat table could not name) matches regardless of node. Consumers: dlm_page_load (ex record at ~1362: purge list instead of import; shared bits at ~1381 with node = slot_node_cb(slot) = the LIVE occupant) → lazy `mxfs_dlm_ledger_purge_owner(ctx, purge[i].node, purge[i].slot)` after the import — a platter write retiring the live node's records. Reproduced deterministically: dlm_ledger_test 7b on the unfixed engine — node 33 dies on slot 3 and is purged (group 7); node 44 joins on slot 3, takes EX on R2; on the master's next import 'P-TAUTH-PURGE node=44 slot=3 cleared=1', W's EX granted immediately (expected: blocked by 44's record until a recovery purge).
